races.name: Aalberts Ips Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has fair recent form at this trip on good ground but is a natural hold-up horse operating in a field of closers, meaning he is unlikely to secure the forward position that would suit him best, which tempers confidence in his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Triple P
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field, trained by Easterby and ridden by apprentice Jake Dickson, and holds a clear tactical advantage as the only horse certain to lead; one run to date (fourth at seven furlongs, good) leaves fitness and improvement scope open, but control of the race is his to lose.

runners_data.name: Spruces Due
runners_data.note: Mullineaux's four-year-old has headgear noted and returns after 48 days off, with a modest form line showing a distant twelfth on good and a fourth at Southwell; a hold-up style in a race dominated by closers makes finding a gap against even this modest field a challenge.

runners_data.name: Sakura Impact
runners_data.note: Mrs Leveque's three-year-old was third over a mile on good ground 24 days ago, showing she handles the conditions, and drops back in trip today; her hold-up style is genuine, and she represents one of the classier profiles in the field if she can close from mid-division in a race likely run at a moderate tempo.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: David Barron's three-year-old carries a hood and has been a consistent placer, including a recent second at six furlongs on good; his true hold-up style means he is shown in midfield on the map rather than the rear where he would naturally race, and the style-fit discount applies if the race shape does not generate enough pace to bring him into it late.

runners_data.name: Kohana Nation
runners_data.note: Charles Hills saddles this lightly raced three-year-old with Oisin Orr aboard after a 225-day absence, which is the single biggest unknown in the race; she showed promise when second at Sandown over seven furlongs but is untested at six, unraced on a true flat straight track, and the lengthy layoff combined with a hold-up style in a slow-tempo race creates significant risk.

races.paceDynamic: Triple P is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner novice contest and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good-to-firm ground over Doncaster's straight six. Stoneacre Joe and Brash are natural hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the field contains more closers than the rear can accommodate, meaning neither is likely to race as far back as they ideally would. The remainder of the field — Spruces Due, Sakura Impact and Kohana Nation — are also hold-up in profile, creating a race where the single pace-setter faces little or no early pressure and can control fractions from the front. This shape strongly favours Triple P and any horse capable of racing prominently or tracking the leader through the race, as a steady-to-moderate tempo with one horse controlling the race from the front on fast ground is unlikely to generate the late surge that pure closers depend upon.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Triple P Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P leads without challenge and dictates a controlled pace throughout the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: Triple P, facing no other confirmed front-runner, can set his own fractions on good-to-firm ground and arrive at the final two furlongs with reserves intact; horses tracking him closely will be best placed as the field fails to close from deep positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P goes off too fast under a forcing ride and ties up in the final furlong, leaving a gap for closers.
scenarios.body: A genuine strong pace from the front would compress the finishing straight and allow one of the genuine deep hold-up types to pick up ground; Sakura Impact and Kohana Nation have the profile to benefit if the pace is truly strong rather than controlled.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Stoneacre Joe or Brash overcome their redistributed position and secure a forward berth to track Triple P closely.
scenarios.body: Either horse forcing their way closer to the pace than the map suggests would create a two-horse contest through the final quarter-mile; Stoneacre Joe has good-going course form at the trip and could be dangerous if allowed to race in his preferred position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Kohana Nation, absent 225 days, returns to form sharply under Oisin Orr and outclasses a modest field on ability.
scenarios.body: The Charles Hills runner showed promise when second at Sandown and arrives with an unknown ceiling after a long absence; if the layoff has not blunted her edge, superior ability on good-to-firm could override the tactical disadvantage of a hold-up style.

watchPoints.text: Triple P's gallop — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and conserve energy, the hold-up dominated field behind him may simply lack the pace to reel him in on good-to-firm ground.

Kohana Nation's fitness after 225 days off is the biggest uncertainty in the race; Charles Hills runners can return fresh but the combination of long absence, trip drop to six furlongs and a closer's style in a moderate-pace race is a significant stack of unknowns.

Stoneacre Joe and Brash are both natural hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map — if neither can secure a position closer to the pace than their true style dictates, the race may play out without them ever landing a serious blow.

Doncaster's straight six on good-to-firm is an unforgiving track for hold-up types when the gallop is steady — watch whether any jockey breaks the hold-up mould early and sends their mount forward to track Triple P, as that horse immediately becomes a prime beneficiary of the race shape.

races.name: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap Stakes
7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Yates Drywall Ltd Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mariner
runners_data.note: Best recent form shows a runner-up at 8f on Good ground nine days ago; wears a hood and tongue-tie, stays on well for Jude Fernandes (7lb claim), and his prominent style makes him the natural foil to Super Hit here — how hard he presses the leader will shape the entire race.

runners_data.name: Magic Runner
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old is fresh off a 127-day absence and drops back from 10f handicap company on the all-weather to turf; a natural hold-up horse, he will need a strong gallop to generate the closing run his style demands, which looks far from guaranteed given the likely early tempo.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Flagged as racing out of role at STYLE_FIT 0.93 as a prominent type in what the data describes as a pace-setter's slot, though the form record at 10f on Good clearly backs his front-running credentials — two wins and a third in recent comparable conditions make him the dominant pace influence regardless of the classification caveat.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's eight-year-old has been running in shorter 8f handicaps of late with little success (form -95766), and the step back to 10f on Good may help, but his hold-up style means he is fully dependent on others to create a pace worth chasing — a questionable scenario here.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's five-year-old has a bleak recent record (form -00096) and, though a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, has been placed in midfield on the pace map due to the cluster of hold-up runners; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 reflects how uncomfortable a position change would be, and his raw form offers little optimism regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Steps In Time
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby sends this runner in without a winner from 11 tries over 14 days and the form string includes a U (unseated) over much longer trips — the drop to 10f helps on paper, but as a true hold-up type nudged forward artificially on the map, Steps In Time needs a strong pace and a clean run that this field is unlikely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he should be able to dictate a comfortable, controlled gallop over the 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. Mariner is the only other runner with prominent tendencies, but the remainder — Magic Runner, Cosmos Raj, Whiskey Pete and Steps In Time — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the early tempo is almost entirely in Super Hit's hands and is unlikely to be severe. That uncontested lead creates a race that shapes as a controlled-pace test where the winner is most likely to come from on or near the pace, as the held-up horses will need a strong enough gallop to close off the final bend and the straight — a gallop that may simply not materialise. This race shape strongly favours prominent and pace-pressing runners who can travel smoothly behind the leader and produce a sustained, grinding finish rather than a sharp late burst. Note that Whiskey Pete and Steps In Time are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the field carries more rear-runners than the map can accommodate at the back; Super Hit and Mariner are the horses most likely to actually secure their natural positions at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Super Hit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit is allowed to bowl along in front without any pressure and the pace stays honest enough only to suit those on or near the lead.
scenarios.body: Super Hit sets a sustainable gallop, the hold-up horses are never given enough to aim at off the final turn, and the runner-up is most likely Mariner, who can track the pace and mount the closest challenge down the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Pressers Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Mariner pushes Super Hit harder than expected in the early stages, lifting the tempo into a proper end-to-end test.
scenarios.body: A contested pace stretches the field sooner and the race becomes a stamina examination, suiting any prominent horse who can handle a stronger gallop and still finish on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Flourish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to set up a strong closing run for the hold-up horses sweeping through from midfield.
scenarios.body: Magic Runner or Cosmos Raj, tracking in behind a fast-run race, find room in the straight and reel in a tiring front-runner; however this requires a genuinely strong pace that looks unlikely given Super Hit's uncontested position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Whiskey Pete or Steps In Time — true hold-up horses placed artificially into a midfield position — manage to find a tactical spot that suits them better than their mapping suggests.
scenarios.body: Racing nearer the pace than usual could help one of them save ground into the home straight and pick up late, though their natural instinct to drop back means the position advantage may be quickly surrendered.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit — if he hacks along unchallenged in front and the sectionals are slow through the first half-mile, the hold-up horses will have nothing to close off and he could prove very hard to peg back in the straight.

Mariner — watch whether Jude Fernandes (7lb claim) elects to challenge Super Hit for the lead or settles in behind; if Mariner pushes forward and tests the pace, the entire complexion of the race changes and the hold-up horses get a much better race shape.

Magic Runner — a 127-day absence is a significant flag; James Sullivan will need to produce a peak fitness performance on the horse's first run since the all-weather, and a hold-up style in a race that may not produce a strong gallop makes this a difficult task.

Cosmos Raj — at age eight and on a losing streak over shorter trips than this, any market move for David O'Meara's runner on the step back to 10f on Good to Firm is worth noting as it may reflect stable confidence in the distance switch.

Steps In Time and Whiskey Pete — both are genuine hold-up horses mapped forward on the pace map; if either tries to race closer than their natural style, watch for them to drift back once the race settles, confirming that the true rear of the field is more congested than the map suggests.

races.name: Winners Wear Skopes Menswear Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Haaderr
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will set the pace throughout; trainer Bethell sends him here 17 days after a fourth at Goodwood, and his three prior placed efforts at 7f on Good ground suggest he handles conditions well — blinkers and tongue-tie fitted, and his ability to dictate will be his primary asset.

runners_data.name: Suspicious Mindz
runners_data.note: Arrives 35 days fresh after a convincing 6f Good ground win and brings strong placed form at 7f and 8f, suggesting the trip holds no fears; Shay Farmer (5) takes the ride and this horse has the form credentials to make the most of sitting second to Haaderr and picking up off the steady pace.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner by inclination who has produced his best form racing prominently, but with Haaderr set to occupy the lead and Suspicious Mindz likely tracking, he is more likely to settle in midfield than he would naturally prefer — Fahey's yard is 1/45 over 14 days and he was last seen 14 days ago; his 7f Good ground record shows consistency at placing level.

runners_data.name: Vidmiyr
runners_data.note: Candlish's 3yo won over 7f on Good ground earlier in the campaign and has the profile to press forward, but the crowded early positions mean he is likely to be further back than ideal; apprentice Jude Fernandes (7) claims 7lb, and Vidmiyr's form over 7-8f on Good gives him place claims at worst if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Goldwork
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer stepping back from 7f to run on Good to Firm ground where he has placed at 6f repeatedly — the tongue bar is fitted and he ran just seven days ago, which is worth monitoring for freshness; needs the pace to be genuine to get competitive, which looks unlikely in this small field.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Longest absent runner in the field at 59 days, and all five recent runs have come at 5-6f, making this 7f trip on Good to Firm a significant question mark; O'Neill takes the ride for Scott Dixon and, as a genuine hold-up type, Shadow Run needs both the step up in trip to suit and a stronger gallop than Haaderr is likely to set.

races.paceDynamic: Haaderr is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field, is set to control this 7f Good to Firm Doncaster contest from the front at a sustainable, unflustered gallop. Suspicious Mindz is the only other natural prominent horse likely to sit close to Haaderr throughout, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly pressured or frantic. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure those positions — First Time and Vidmiyr are both natural prominent racers but are mapped to midfield because Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz will occupy the limited space near the head of affairs. With a steady, controlled tempo over a flat 7f on quick ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit close to the pace and sustain their effort into the straight — the prominent-to-lead profile is the one to be on, as hold-up horses Goldwork and Shadow Run are likely to find the gallop too modest for them to produce a decisive late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Haaderr Controls, Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr leads at a sustainable clip and Suspicious Mindz tracks in second without forcing a faster pace, the race becomes a procession for those closest to the front.
scenarios.body: Haaderr dictates every yard on Good to Firm ground, setting a rhythm that suits those on the pace, and the lack of pressure means the leader can conserve enough energy to repel any late challenge up the straight; Suspicious Mindz, tracking in second, is ideally positioned to pounce if Haaderr falters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If First Time or Vidmiyr manage to press closer than their mapped midfield position and competitive enough fractions develop to bring them into the finish.
scenarios.body: Good to Firm conditions and a flat 7f track at Doncaster suit both horses' natural prominent style, and if they can find their preferred ground near the pace rather than being shuffled back, their form figures at the trip are competitive enough to threaten; however this scenario is constrained by the likelihood that Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz will occupy those early positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated, Haaderr becomes pressured, and the tempo is fast enough to set up a late run for the hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Goldwork and Shadow Run would need a genuine end-to-end gallop to generate the momentum for a late flourish, but with only one confirmed front-runner and a small six-runner field, a true strong pace is unlikely to materialise; both are untested at 7f, and Goldwork's 6f form suggests the extra furlong may not fully play to their strengths.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that the field bunches and the finish becomes a scramble, favouring any horse with a turn of foot from any position.
scenarios.body: An extreme slow burn is possible in theory with just one front-runner and six runners, but Good to Firm ground typically encourages a more even pace at Doncaster; if the race does fall apart into a sprint finish, any of the prominent horses tracking the leader could benefit simply by being handiest.

watchPoints.text: Haaderr is the lone front-runner and if he gets loose on a fast surface he could prove very difficult to reel in — watch for whether Suspicious Mindz or any other runner exerts early pressure that could compromise the leader's rhythm.

First Time and Vidmiyr are both natural prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace — watch the early stages to see whether either can force their way into the front rank or whether they are indeed shuffled to midfield as their redistribution flags suggest.

Shadow Run's step up from 5-6f to 7f after a 59-day absence is a significant combination of unknowns — watch the betting market for any sign the stable has the horse forward enough to justify confidence at the longer trip.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for the 4:15 at Doncaster — Goldwork holds headgear (tongue bar) and has run just seven days ago; monitor whether the quick ground and short turnaround leave him below his best in the straight.

races.name: Harrison College Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places in her last five at 7f on Good ground including a recent victory, making her the most consistent hold-up performer at this trip and going; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a practical advantage and she sets the benchmark for finishing form here.

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: David Nolan takes the ride on a horse who has been placed three times recently but is a genuine closer naturally suited to a stronger gallop than this race is likely to serve up; Paul Midgley's stable is 1 from 19 over 14 days, so form angle is quiet.

runners_data.name: Operation Gimcrack
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and likely to get a free, uncontested lead; five efforts at 7f including a Southwell win show he can do it at the trip, though his course-and-distance form on Good is limited and he has raced infrequently for Smart's yard recently.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old is equipped with a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse by nature; his recent form string of 760787 is uninspiring and his seven-furlong efforts on Good ground have not produced a placing, with his natural style leaving him dependent on a strong pace that is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Queensmaite
runners_data.note: Returning from a 95-day absence for the modest S R Bowring yard, which has yet to fire a winner in the past 14 days; a natural closer who will need to come from the pack, her recent form on Good ground at 5f-7f has been weak and the long break adds risk.

runners_data.name: Danrana
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with a warning flag for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern in a race likely to produce a steadily-run contest where any weakness in the home straight is punished; Fionn McSharry's yard is quiet, and her 63-day absence adds to the cautionary read.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Pink
runners_data.note: Has placed four times in her last five outings on Good ground, including a win, and her headgear note of 'p' (probably a hood or visor) suggests she responds well to restraint; Ryan Sexton takes the ride and, unusually for this field, she has a genuine finishing kick that suits a race run at a modest tempo.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has been placed six times in his last fifteen outings on Good ground but has not won; James Sullivan rides a horse who will naturally come from behind, and while his consistency at 7f on Good is solid, the redistributed position means he is unlikely to get the clean run his style demands.

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is firing on six winners from 88 runners over 14 days, making this one of the stronger trainer angles in the race; Jake Dickson's 5lb claim helps, and his win at 6f on Good ground recently shows he acts on the surface, though stepping to 7f for the first time and being a natural hold-up horse in a steady-pace race tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Carries a dual warning — a tendency to fade late and a tongue-tie — and is returning from 58 days off for Lawrence Mullaney's yard, which has not struck in the past fortnight; a genuine hold-up type whose form figures (095-88) are poor, and the combination of flags makes him a hard proposition in this shape.

runners_data.name: Havana Oaks
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old has four career runs and no wins, with form of 55-67 suggesting she has not progressed; Joey Haynes rides a horse who is a natural closer that has only managed one effort on Good ground, and with the lowest weight in the race (124lbs) she is lightly weighted but has given no signs yet of being competitive at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Operation Gimcrack is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap at Doncaster on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine pace rival to press him, he is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the front without being harassed. The bulk of this field — Moonhall Lass, Get Up Everybody, Arnaz, Queensmaite, Emerald Army, Hares Bredth, Ryefield, and Havana Oaks — are all natural hold-up or off-the-pace types, meaning the race is likely to develop into a steadily-run contest with a large, bunched pack tracking Operation Gimcrack at a manageable tempo. Several redistributed hold-up horses — most notably Hares Bredth, Get Up Everybody, and Arnaz — are genuine closers who will not naturally secure a prominent berth, so the pack behind Operation Gimcrack will be dense and positional scrimmaging is likely through the early stages. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in mid-division and produce a sustained finish on fast ground, rather than true deep closers who need a stronger gallop to reel the front-runner in — a prominent-to-midfield profile with finishing ability is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gimcrack Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Operation Gimcrack dictates an unchallenged, controlled tempo and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Operation Gimcrack, uncontested at the front, sets fractions that are sustainable at 7f on quick ground, and with the chasing pack congested and unable to build momentum off a steady gallop, he simply has too much in hand turning in. Prominent or close-tracking types who can get within striking distance early are best placed to challenge, but may just find the leader has stolen enough of a break.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently just behind Operation Gimcrack picks him off in the final furlong without needing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop means stamina is not truly tested, so a horse sitting second or third and travelling well can simply produce a clean, sustained challenge rather than a sprint burst. Moonhall Lass and Sparkling Pink, both capable of tracking close to the pace on this going, are best suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves quicker than expected or the field fans wide in the straight, allowing true hold-up horses to finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop, or a wide-open straight at Doncaster, could allow redistributed hold-up types like Hares Bredth and Emerald Army to get competitive late, but their repositioned roles and the likely steady tempo make this a less probable shape. Even if closers do finish well, many are racing out of their natural position and may lack the momentum needed to catch the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a wall of horses hits the front simultaneously, causing a chaotic pace collapse and an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types redistributed into midfield, a bunched, scrappy race where several horses lose their footing tactically is possible, producing a messy finish. In such a scenario, a horse able to find a clear run from any position — Sparkling Pink or Arnaz — might benefit from getting daylight at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Operation Gimcrack is the sole front-runner in a field of hold-up horses — if he steals even two lengths of daylight in the early stages unchallenged, the congested pack behind may simply lack the pace to reel him in on quick ground.

Hares Bredth is a natural hold-up horse backed by a strong Easterby trainer angle and a capable claimer, but she is stepping up to 7f for the first time and will need to find a clear run from a position she may not naturally achieve — watch for her getting boxed in.

Danrana and Ryefield both carry stamina/finishing fade warnings and are returning from lengthy breaks (63 and 58 days respectively) — if the pace collapses they are at serious risk of dropping away sharply in the final furlong.

Sparkling Pink's headgear and recent placed form on Good ground make her one of the more tractable hold-up types in the field — watch to see if Ryan Sexton moves her up sooner than expected to exploit the steady gallop rather than settling deep.

With so many redistributed closers packed into midfield, the race draw and early positioning in the first two furlongs will be critical — horses drawn high or slow away risk being locked on the inner with nowhere to go on Doncaster's straight seven.

races.name: Harrison College Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Consistent at 5f on good ground earlier this season but steps up sharply to 7f here, a trip he has not raced over in this form cycle, and his hold-up style from the rear leaves him dependent on a strong gallop that this pace map does not guarantee.

runners_data.name: Wilde And Dandy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with three places from fifteen starts at 7f on good ground, suggesting course-trip combination is understood, though his natural hold-up style places him in midfield here where he races away from his best position; Joey Haynes must be positive early to compensate.

runners_data.name: Groundsman
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a natural closer who finds himself mapped into midfield due to pace overcrowding; Mark Loughnane's charge has shown nothing in two recent starts on good ground at 7f, and until that form changes the style compromise compounds an already thin profile.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Posted a runner-up finish at 7f on soft and retains ability on a sounder surface, but the fades-in-finish flag is a genuine concern at this trip, and Nigel Tinkler's runner is a true hold-up horse displaced into a midfield position that will not suit if the pace is steady.

runners_data.name: Barbuda Bay
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 49 days and also flagged as a finisher who fades, two compounding negatives; Roger Teal's three-year-old is a hold-up horse relocated to midfield and has only one comparable-going effort in five recorded runs, making ground conditions an additional uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: The most interesting position play in the race — a three-year-old for Michael and David Easterby whose recent form includes a runner-up at 6f on good, and whose natural style sits just off the pace, meaning Oliver Stammers can tuck in directly behind Back From Dubai and inherit the best ground in the race.

runners_data.name: Sprinting Speed
runners_data.note: Carries the fades-in-finish warning and has not threatened in seven outings on similar going, with Jennie Candlish's filly yet to win; the hold-up profile and modest form line makes this a difficult winner to construct under any scenario.

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: The fulcrum of the entire race — a nine-year-old for S R Bowring who won over 7f on soft and placed at this trip on good, dropping to a career-low OR 51 and guaranteed an uncontested lead by the absence of any other confirmed front-runner; Alistair Rawlinson simply needs to let him bowl along at his own pace.

runners_data.name: Magic Lady Mae
runners_data.note: Jack Gilligan takes the ride on Lawrence Mullaney's three-year-old, who has run just 11 days ago and steps onto good ground having no comparable going evidence in seven career starts; she is a hold-up horse competing out of her natural position with the thinnest going profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Mister McGregor
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 7f including a third at Doncaster itself, so track and trip combination has some relevance for M Mullineaux's four-year-old; he is a natural closer mapped to midfield through redistribution, but that Doncaster placing shows the course suits and Kieran O'Neill will need to be clever to manufacture a run from a compromised position.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride clear from the gates and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Doncaster's straight seven furlongs on good-to-firm ground. The pace will be honest but not frenetic — a lone pace-setter at OR 51 in a field of OR 56-60 rivals is unlikely to be chased hard early, meaning the fractions will be measured and the leader will conserve energy for the finish. The overwhelming majority of the field are natural hold-up horses, but with so many closers present and only one horse setting the pace from the front, late runners face a genuine tactical problem: there may not be enough early speed to generate a strong enough pull for an effective finishing surge. This shape strongly favours the lone pace-setter and any horse capable of travelling prominently in second or third without expending energy, rather than true closers who need a genuine gallop to pick up off — the field holds far more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in their natural role, with Barbuda Bay, Wilde And Dandy, Groundsman, Sir David, Magic Lady Mae and Mister McGregor all redistributed from genuine hold-up positions into the midfield map; Back From Dubai is most likely to secure the rail and the lead unchallenged, with Von Trotter best placed to take a prominent second position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a controlled, measured pace that suits a front-runner on this flat, straight track.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai has already won at 7f on soft going and is dropping dramatically in class at OR 51, and with no rival willing or able to press it early it simply dictates from flag to finish on a course that does not bend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned second or third behind Back From Dubai tracks the leader smoothly and quickens past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace means a prominent horse travelling kindly behind the leader will have energy in reserve to accelerate, exploiting Back From Dubai if it ties up near the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Gets Lucky Split
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a well-positioned midfield horse finds a gap to exploit in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A truly slow early gallop occasionally concertinas the field enough for a sharp finisher to weave through, though with so many redistributed hold-up types occupying midfield this scenario relies on horses racing out of their natural role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp the Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai sets a faster than expected pace that drains itself, triggering a late sweep from genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires conditions that do not obviously exist here — a lone front-runner at OR 51 has every incentive to conserve energy, and the true closers have been shuffled out of their natural positions, making a mass late surge the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai holds an uncontested lead in a field of closers — watch whether Alistair Rawlinson controls the gallop completely or lets it drift fast, as that single decision shapes every other outcome in the race.

Von Trotter's ability to slot directly behind Back From Dubai in second position is critical — if Oliver Stammers secures that spot cleanly, he inherits the tactical advantage that every other runner will be competing for.

Wilde And Dandy, Groundsman, Sir David, Barbuda Bay and Magic Lady Mae are all natural hold-up horses displaced into midfield; watch for early crowding and jostling as multiple riders attempt to find positions that the pace map cannot comfortably accommodate.

The going is Good To Firm throughout the card at Doncaster despite the race card listing Good — all runners are assessed on that faster surface, which particularly benefits horses with confirmed good-to-firm form and may catch out any runner whose best form came on a softer surface.

Mister McGregor has a recorded placing at Doncaster over 7f, giving him specific course-and-distance evidence that most rivals lack — watch whether Kieran O'Neill uses that familiarity to find an economical route through from midfield.

races.name: Grace And Dotty Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer in form — placed at 5f and 6f on Good recently — but at age 10 and off a 26-day break, will need a genuinely strong pace to close from the back, which this shape may not provide; Oliver Stammers takes over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Shazani
runners_data.note: Trainer Bowring winless in 3 recent runners and this 4yo has struggled on Good ground historically (0W2P in similar conditions); a true deep hold-up horse whose natural finishing position is compressed by the volume of closers in this field, limiting its opportunity.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3yo ran only 11 days ago and showed a win and a second at 6f on Good — the form is live — but its hold-up instincts are likely suppressed here as it pushes forward to avoid being trapped in a slow-pace cavalry charge; headgear noted (visor).

runners_data.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners_data.note: Has finished 8th, 9th or 10th in five recent starts including a sequence on Good ground, with both cheekpieces and tongue-tie in use; a hold-up type whose 6f form at this level has been poor, and the style redistribution further undermines its prospects.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: William Knight's 3yo has a win and four places from recent starts and ran well at 6f on Good — the sharpest form line among the hold-up contingent — and may trade her natural rear position for a more prominent one given the pace scenario; Neil Callan's experience is a plus.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: The one genuine prominent runner outside Ziggy's Condor; Julie Camacho's 3yo has placed twice at 6f and should track the leader throughout — Good To Firm suits and a 31-day break is not a concern given its recent consistency, though sim-going record reads 0W1P in four outings.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 7yo has placed twice at 6f on Good but carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and is OR-highest alongside Ziggy's Condor at 70 — softer ground form is poor; Alex Jary (3lb claim) may not offset the finishing concern in a race where a slow early pace kills the hold-up chance.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's 5yo is the sole front-runner and ran just 3 days ago — fitness is not in doubt but freshness of recovery may be; the blinkers are retained and Good To Firm Doncaster over 6f suits a pace-setting role, though its recent record shows no wins and a U completion, tempering confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy's Condor is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 6f Good To Firm Doncaster handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off — a pace scenario that suits horses capable of tracking rather than those needing a strong tempo to close into. Celtic Arrow is the only other runner with prominent credentials and will likely settle just off Ziggy's Condor's quarters, giving the leader a comfortable buffer against the bulk of the field. The remainder — Mark's Choice, Shazani, Come On Over, Ay Gee Ell, Startled Lady, and Another Investment — are all hold-up types by inclination, but the field holds far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate; of those, Come On Over and Startled Lady show the pace figures and recent form to suggest they are most likely to push forward and secure a better position than their natural style implies. With one front-runner setting a measured pace on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours the close-tracking prominent profile — a horse able to sit just off the controlled pace and pounce in the final furlong without needing a gruelling test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ziggy Dictates Controlled Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a fair but manageable clip, setting a steady rhythm throughout.
scenarios.body: Ziggy's Condor rolls through the first three furlongs unchallenged, taking all the kick out of a slow early pace and leaving little for true hold-up horses to close into; Celtic Arrow, tracking throughout, is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and a horse positioned second or third sweeps past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Celtic Arrow or Startled Lady, tracking within a length of the leader, exploit the fast ground to finish powerfully once Ziggy's Condor's early effort takes its toll; the Good To Firm surface rewards horses with a clean stride cycle from a handy position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor sets a stronger pace than expected and the race develops into a proper test that opens up ground for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Mark's Choice or Another Investment, back-pedalling early, find the pace quick enough to produce a true run and close relentlessly in the final 2f; this shape is less likely given the redistribution note — most of the nominal hold-up horses are likely to race closer than their mapped positions, reducing the gap for genuine closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor bowls along and the hold-up horses, racing out of role in a compressed field, fail to organise a meaningful challenge.
scenarios.body: Ziggy's Condor, left alone on a sound surface at a pace entirely of its own choosing, simply never gets caught; at 3 days since its last run the fitness query is real, but the tactical advantage of a lone lead on Good To Firm Doncaster turf is significant.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy's Condor's 3-day turnaround is unusually quick — watch to see if it breaks sharply and commands the lead cleanly, or if it is slow away, which would trigger an entirely different pace shape.

Celtic Arrow is the key pace tracker: if it slots in second without pressure in the first furlong, the race is likely to play out as a two-horse break-away from the pack and will heavily favour prominent runners.

Come On Over and Startled Lady — both natural hold-up horses — may push forward early to avoid getting marooned in a slow pace; watch for a scrimmage across the first 2f as redistributed closers scramble for position.

Another Investment's fade-in-finish flag is worth monitoring on Good To Firm — if the pace is slow and the race develops into a sprint, its stamina concern is amplified; it has placed twice at this course and distance but only when the race truly tests.

Mark's Choice at age 10 is the longest-in-the-tooth runner and needs everything to go right — a genuine pace and a clean run — so watch whether Oliver Stammers elects to ride handier than his natural hold-up profile would suggest.
